properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-09-14, thinking out loud about seed templates and what Alex hit at work.

═══ WHAT PROMPTED IT ═══

Alex's agent could not work out what his project's "systems" were in SE terms and handed the question back to him — asking what a *query* was — and his translator answered "Interface". `dec:idea-a-users-domain-vocabulary-has-no-route-into-se-vocabulary` argues the hard part is ROUTING, not coverage: Interface, Capability, Requirement and Flow are all defensible for that word and lead to different designs. `dec:idea-the-routing-table-routes-grammar-not-domain-nouns` sharpens it — the shipped table routes ENGLISH PHRASING and Alex's question is about NOUNS.

Anthony's move: ask about functions (black boxes) and interfaces in a way that needs no SE knowledge — and then KEEP the answers.

═══ THE IDEA, in his words ═══

"a follow-on set of questions (if it isn't immediately clear to the agent) is to have some set of questions where the agent asks about functions (black boxes) and interfaces without the user having to know systems engineering. These would go into the design 'template' for the project that help explain to an agent and becomes a reference for all future users what the functions and interfaces are."

Two halves, and the second is the new one:

**(i) A FOLLOW-ON QUESTION SET, FIRED ON AMBIGUITY.** The five interview questions in capture-intent already ask about the thing rather than the schema (cap:the-design-interview-precedes-the-capture, realized). What does not exist is a SECOND pass that fires when the first leaves the routing genuinely ambiguous — the exact state Alex's agent was in when it gave up and asked him. There is no defined behaviour today for "the interview ran and I still cannot route this": the skill forbids handing the question back, and says nothing about what to do instead.

**(ii) ⭐ THE ANSWERS BECOME A DURABLE PROJECT ARTEFACT.** Today the interview's output dissolves into nodes and the interview itself is forgotten. The proposal is that "in THIS project, a function is X, an interface is Y, and here is what we call them" survives as a reference — read by the next agent and the next person, instead of being re-derived or re-asked.

═══ WHY THIS MIGHT BE THE RIGHT SHAPE ═══

It lands on option (c) of BOTH older questions — a per-project glossary the design holds — but arrives from a third direction. Those two reached it by asking what to do with a translator somebody had already written. This reaches it by asking what the interview should have KEPT. Three independent routes to one mechanism is weak evidence, but it is evidence.

It also has a partial home already: record_alias puts the user's own noun on a node, and capture-intent instructs it. That is the per-NODE case. This is the per-CATEGORY case — what the TYPES mean here, not what one thing is called.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) Nothing new. record_alias plus the interview covers it.** ⚠️ Counter: aliases attach to nodes that already exist. Alex's failure was upstream of any node — he could not get the FIRST one created.

**(b) A second interview pass that fires on ambiguity; output captured as ordinary nodes.** Cheapest, and the half with a clear failure behind it. ⚠️ Counter: answers (i) and not (ii) — the reasoning still dissolves and the next session re-asks.

**(c) A project-level reference the interview WRITES — the design's own SE glossary.** ⚠️ Counter: real vocabulary surface, all three legs, on an n=1 report; and it can freeze an early wrong call into something that reads authoritative.

**(d) Fold it into the seed template instead.** A domain seed (dec:idea-a-domain-seed-template-starts-a-design-in-the-fields-own-shape) could ARRIVE carrying "what a function and an interface are in this field", and the interview only fills gaps. ⚠️ Counter: helps only designs whose domain has a template, which is none of them today.

═══ ⚠️ THE COUNTERWEIGHT ═══

**A glossary that is wrong is worse than no glossary**, because it is inherited without being re-examined. Alex's translator calling a query an Interface may be a category error; this idea's effect would be to make that call permanent and authoritative for every future session on his project. The older question already says nothing in reflow2 can tell him which is right — and making the answer DURABLE does not make it CORRECT. Whatever is built here needs to be overturnable as cheaply as it is written.
properties.name: OPEN — should the design interview's ANSWERS become a project-level reference every later session inherits, and what asks the follow-on questions when the first pass is not clear?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an open question rather than a proposal, via the brainstorm discipline. Kept separate from the /template-skill question and the two-pass-extraction question because they fail differently: this is about what the interview KEEPS, the second about what the user can DECLARE, the third about how a description is PARSED.
